newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept housing starts fell 6.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept housing starts fell 6.0 percent.

Unadjusted Actual Starts and Permits, in 1,000s:
Wall Street economists had forecast September starts at a 1.47 million unit annual rate.
The department said the 6.0 percent drop in September housing starts was the largest decline since January 1995's 9.0 percent drop.
The department said September single-family starts fell 8.9 percent to an annual rate of 1.122 million units.
The department revised July starts to a 1.3 percent drop to an annual rate of 1.470 million units. Previously, it said July starts fell 2.0 percent to a 1.460 million unit annual rate.
July permits were unrevised at a 3.0 percent rise to an annual rate of 1.457 million units.
